analysis.scope_and_question: Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) is one of the least studied species within the genus Orthoebolavirus (family Filoviridae), despite its capacity to cause severe Ebola virus disease (EVD) with substantial mortality.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review, not a systematic review or meta-analysis, summarizes peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and official situation reports from WHO, Africa CDC, US CDC, ECDC, and national health ministries, identified through PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Embase from inception to 12 August 2026, to examine BDBV historical evolution, virology and pathogenesis, drivers of re-emergence, surveillance and response, therapeutic and vaccine gaps, and global health security implications.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of active case finding, surveillance cascade and response bottlenecks during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, highlighting the need for improved surveillance and response mechanisms to rapidly interrupt ebolavirus transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective descriptive ecological analysis was conducted using the national situation-report series from the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the DRC, with chronology and operational context triangulated against official WHO and Africa CDC reports. The study included 5,713 confirmed cases and 2,744 confirmed deaths across 58 health zones in six provinces by 25 August 2026.
analysis.methods: The analysis used a primary national-first date-level hierarchy to identify 71 qualifying reporting observations. It applied strict source-linkability rules without imputation and examined process indicators such as alert-investigation coverage, sampling coverage, validation yield, contact follow-up and point-of-entry/point-of-control screening.
analysis.main_results: By 25 August 2026, 96 out of 103 expected report positions were available, yielding 2,375 source-derived records. Median cumulative alert-investigation coverage was 88.5% (IQR 79.9–94.2; n=97), sampling coverage 66.7% (IQR 54.5–74.6; n=5), validation yield 26.0% (IQR 20.2–74.2; n=35), contact follow-up 78.2% (IQR 67.3–82.9; n=90), and point-of-entry/point-of-control screening approximately 98.0% (IQR 96.0–98.8; n=32).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that contact follow-up was the lowest measured process in 55 observations (77.5%), followed by alert investigation in 12 (16.9%), sampling in three (4.2%) and point-of-entry/point-of-control screening in one (1.4%). This highlights the need for strengthening these processes to improve early detection and limit community transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of strengthening contact follow-up, active case-finding capacity, field logistics, community trust and safe access to enhance surveillance, accelerate diagnosis and care, and limit continued community transmission of ebolavirus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on public reporting, which did not consistently link validated or sampled alerts to same-cohort Ebola treatment centre transfer. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the effectiveness of active case finding, surveillance cascade and response bottlenecks during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It highlights the critical role of surveillance in rapidly interrupting ebolavirus transmission and identifies contact follow-up as the dominant recurrent bottleneck. The analysis, based on national situation reports and official WHO and Africa CDC data, reveals that while most process indicators were high, contact follow-up and alert investigation had notable gaps. The study underscores the need for strengthening these processes, along with field logistics and community trust, to improve early detection and limit community transmission. However, the reliance on public reporting introduces limitations, as it may not fully capture the operational details of the outbreak response.

analysis.summary_en: Background Antibody-based therapies have become a cornerstone of Ebola virus disease (EVD) treatment and prevention, particularly following the successful clinical development of monoclonal antibody therapeutics against Zaire ebolavirus. Methods Publications related to antibody therapy for EVD published between 1990 and 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, and Scopus databases. Following data integration, format conversion, and deduplication, a total of 1,350 unique publications were included. Keyword co-occurrence and clustering analyses revealed five major thematic domains: fundamental virology and glycoprotein research, immunity and vaccination, infection and therapeutic development, cross-viral research involving COVID-19 and HIV, and clinically oriented studies focused on neutralizing antibodies, clinical trials, and convalescent plasma. The current Bundibugyo outbreak highlights persistent vulnerabilities in existing countermeasure strategies and emphasizes the urgent need for broadly protective pan-ebolavirus antibody therapeutics. Conclusions Ebola antibody therapy research has undergone substantial expansion over the past three decades, driven largely by major outbreak events and advances in antibody engineering technologies.

title: Field Investigation of the Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease (BDBV) Outbreak in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo: Challenges, Strategies, and Priority Actions for Outbreak Control—An Outbreak Investigation Review

analysis.scope_and_question: The 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BDBV) in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), centered in Ituri Province, represents the largest documented outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus since its discovery in Uganda in 2007. The field investigation aimed to assess epidemiological, operational, laboratory, infection prevention and control (IPC), community engagement, risk communication, and infodemic management challenges and identify priority interventions to strengthen outbreak control.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A rapid field assessment was conducted between 12–15 June 2026 in Bunia, Rwampara Health Zone, and the Ituri Provincial Public Health Laboratory. Data were collected through direct observation, review of surveillance and laboratory reports, health facility assessments, stakeholder interviews, and analysis of outbreak response indicators.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: As of 12 July 2026, the outbreak had resulted in 1926 laboratory-confirmed cases and 702 deaths, corresponding to an overall case fatality rate (CFR) of 36.4% across affected provinces. Ituri Province remained the epicenter, accounting for 90.8% of confirmed cases (1705/1877) and 85.5% of reported deaths (577/675). Risk communication and community engagement efforts were constrained by limited outreach capacity, language barriers, low trust, and inadequate systems for rumor detection and infodemic response.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Contact tracing remained a major challenge, with only 64.4% (4171/6475) of registered contacts successfully followed, below the recommended ≥95% target. Major operational challenges included limited treatment capacity, high occupancy of Ebola treatment centres, shortages of trained personnel and IPC supplies, insecurity affecting response teams, and insufficient preparedness in newly affected areas. Data inconsistencies, delayed investigations, and gaps in outcome classification affected response monitoring.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Sustained transmission, community deaths, geographic expansion, and operational constraints highlight the urgent need to strengthen surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory systems, IPC capacity, clinical care, and integrated risk communication and infodemic management strategies. Building trust through community-centered approaches, proactive misinformation management, and engagement of trusted local actors will be essential to accelerate outbreak containment and strengthen preparedness across the Great Lakes region.

analysis.summary_en: This review article presents a field investigation of the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. The outbreak, which occurred in a complex humanitarian setting marked by conflict, displacement, and weak health systems, resulted in 1926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths, with a case fatality rate of 36.4%. Ituri Province was the epicenter, accounting for 90.8% of cases and 85.5% of deaths. The study highlights challenges in contact tracing, with only 64.4% of contacts successfully followed, and operational issues such as limited treatment capacity, shortages of personnel and supplies, and insecurity. Risk communication and community engagement were hindered by language barriers, low trust, and inadequate systems for managing misinformation. The article emphasizes the need for improved surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory systems, and integrated risk communication strategies, alongside building trust through community-centered approaches. These findings underscore the difficulties of controlling Ebola outbreaks in conflict-affected and socially complex environments.

title: Communication is not consultation: a documentary analysis of participation depth and the architecture of community engagement during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

analysis.research_question_and_background: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) is treated as essential to Ebola response, but routine reporting can collapse qualitatively different forms of participation into a single category of "engagement." We examined what kinds of participation were actually demonstrable in the documentary record of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), and what the reporting system itself made visible.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The response nevertheless possessed a substantial listening apparatus: community concerns included treatment-centre conditions, delayed safe and dignified burials, alert handling, decontamination, medicines, vaccines, clinical trials and body presentation.
analysis.methods: We conducted a documentary analysis of national outbreak SitReps and companion RCCE streams through 3 September 2026. Exact source excerpts, actors, dates, sources and validation status were retained. The frozen primary dataset comprised 180 RCCE documentary units; 156 were validated directly to source PDF/text and physical page, and 24 late-window units were verified to the processed national stream pending original-page validation.
analysis.main_results: Thirty units (16.7%) were information, 111 (61.7%) sensitisation/mobilisation, 37 (20.6%) feedback collection, and two (1.1%) consultation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The 2026 response record documents extensive communication, mobilisation and social listening, but makes community influence over response decisions much less observable.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: RCCE monitoring should therefore complement reach metrics with explicit feedback-uptake and decision-trace indicators.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The documentary chain usually ended at feedback capture, clarification or exchange rather than a traceable decision-to-modification pathway.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the forms of community participation during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BDBV) response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). It highlights that while extensive communication and mobilisation were documented, community influence over decision-making was less visible. The research uses a documentary analysis of outbreak SitReps and RCCE streams, identifying different levels of participation. The findings suggest that current RCCE monitoring should include indicators of feedback uptake and decision-traceability. The study's limitations include the endpoint of the documentary chain at feedback capture rather than decision modification. The evidence is strong as it is based on direct analysis of the primary dataset.

title: The social production of epidemic data: response contestation, institutional disruption and surveillance observability during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo — a longitudinal documentary analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Epidemic surveillance is often represented as a technical pipeline converting cases, contacts, specimens and deaths into data. Sociology of quantification and Ebola social-science research suggest instead that the conditions for observation are socially and institutionally produced.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We examine this during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Methods: We conducted longitudinal documentary analysis and within-case process tracing using Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) situation reports and operational indicators.
analysis.methods: Candidate mentions were collapsed into unique episodes; event date was separated from report date; source labels such as 'resistance' were preserved but not treated as explanations; and core classification required a documented consequence for access, investigation, sampling, burial, screening, isolation or reporting.
analysis.main_results: The analytic set was frozen at 1 September 2026; narrative streams were checked through 3 September for carry-forward and resolution. Forty-six unique episodes were retained: 22 core observability events, 22 supporting disruptions without a demonstrated observation loss, and two ambiguous events.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Observability was disrupted through heterogeneous mechanisms and actors, including armed-group and protest-related access constraints, community refusal, attacks on burial teams, provider strikes and non-payment, protocol refusal by humanitarian or military personnel, patient escapes, delayed team arrival, and security decisions releasing bodies before sampling.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Surveillance systems should preserve structured metadata on non-observation, actor, mechanism and restoration to better distinguish absence of disease from absence of observation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific statistical analyses or numerical findings about the effectiveness of surveillance interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the social and institutional factors influencing epidemic data production during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It challenges the notion of surveillance as a purely technical process, highlighting how social dynamics and institutional responses shape the observability of outbreaks. The research employed longitudinal documentary analysis and process tracing using INSP reports to identify 46 unique episodes, including 22 core observability events and 22 disruptions without observation loss. The findings reveal that data gaps and delays are often due to complex interactions between actors and mechanisms rather than technical failures. The study emphasizes the need for structured metadata to differentiate between absence of disease and absence of observation. While the analysis provides novel insights into the social production of epidemic data, it does not include specific statistical analyses or numerical outcomes.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Uganda met all three 7-1-7 targets: detection within 6 days, notification within <1 day, and response completion within 2 days. The review highlights the cross-border nature of the outbreak, with 15 of 20 confirmed cases imported from the DRC. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that reported case-fatality rates for BVD are generally lower than for Zaire ebolavirus. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for sustained joint surveillance and coordinated screening along the Uganda–DRC corridor. analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the detection, notification, and response timeliness during a cross-border Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2026. It also highlights the absence of a licensed vaccine for BVD and the ongoing development of specific vaccines and therapeutics. The findings suggest the importance of joint efforts between countries to address gaps in outbreak response and preparedness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the risks posed by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to neighboring countries, particularly due to cross-border dynamics and the potential for transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reports on the outbreak confirmed in Ituri Province, DRC, on 15 May 2026, and highlights Uganda's reported cases on the same day in travellers from DRC, indicating cross-border transmission. analysis.methods: The study incorporates consultations with co-authors and reviewers, web searches, and reviews of newspaper coverage to highlight key socioeconomic and political considerations in the South Sudan–DRC borderlands that shape Ebola preparedness and response.
analysis.main_results: Uganda reported cases on the same day in travellers from DRC, highlighting the threat of cross-border transmission driven by porous borders, displacement, conflict and strong social and trade ties.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study focuses on cross-border livelihoods, mobility, security, and healthcare-seeking, with particular attention to preparedness and socioeconomic consequences of cross-border health measures on the South Sudan side of the border.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted context-sensitive interventions at border crossings, along transport routes, and other high-risk locations to address cross-border transmission risks and improve preparedness in the region.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the cross-border dynamics of the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and its implications for neighboring countries, particularly South Sudan. Although South Sudan has not reported cases as of 13 August 2026, it has strengthened preparedness efforts in border regions due to shared borders with DRC and Uganda. The study emphasizes the need for a mobility-sensitive and cross-border approach to Ebola preparedness, incorporating population movements and protection needs. It builds on previous analyses and consultations to highlight key socioeconomic and political factors influencing preparedness and response. The findings suggest that targeted interventions at border crossings and transport routes are essential for mitigating cross-border transmission risks. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence and does not include detailed statistical or laboratory methods, which limits the confidence in its conclusions.

title: Epidemic Comparison of Ebola and Zika-the Only Two Neglected Tropical Diseases with Vertical Transmission Potential and Associated with Public Health Emergency of International Concern-among Childbearing Women.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limited comparative epidemiological evidence on Ebola virus disease (EVD) and Zika virus disease (ZVD) in women of childbearing age (WCBA), which hinders understanding of their mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) potential and maternal–neonatal protection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study compared EVD and ZVD epidemiology in WCBA, focusing on incidence, deaths, years of life lost (YLLs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) from 2011 to 2023. analysis.methods: Cumulative cases, age-standardised incidence rates (ASIRs), and mortality-to-incidence ratios (MIRs) were calculated. Sex-specific differences and correlations between ZVD ASIRs and live births were assessed.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform strengthened EVD monitoring in Sub-Saharan Africa and a Latin America-Caribbean-centred strategy for ZVD prevention targeting WCBA, potentially improving maternal-neonatal protection and control of neglected tropical diseases with MTCT potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on data extracted from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study, which may have limitations in data quality and completeness. The study suggests that targeted prevention strategies for ZVD in WCBA and enhanced EVD monitoring in Sub-Saharan Africa could improve maternal-neonatal protection.
